A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMErroR and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated results can be matched, supporting a reliable comparison despite substantive revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 20 VLMs, annotation agreement, diagnostic experiments, confusion matrices, and few-shot results.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 12 VLMs on the revised benchmark, together with annotation agreement, diagnostic experiments, and appendix few-shot results.

M1.justification: The four error categories, GPT-5 error generation, verification and filtering pipeline, and ETC/EPD procedures remain intact. Appendices A and B retain the same filtering formula and generation prompt. Revised EPD wording clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five source datasets, six domains, 24 subdomains, and ETC, EPD, and auxiliary VQA tasks. Revised sample and category counts change composition within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated roster changes from 20 to 12 VLMs. Kimi-K2.5 and Doubao-Seed-2.0-pro are added; Claude-4-Sonnet and GLM-4.5 are replaced by Claude-Opus-4.5 and GLM-4.6V. Several comparisons disappear, including o4-mini and the Gemini-2.5 models. Doubao also replaces o4-mini in the auxiliary tables.

E3.justification: The reported benchmark changes from 2,013 to 1,997 samples, with revised domain and error-type composition. For example, Physics & Engineering changes from 511 to 459 samples and Earth & Environment from 335 to 393 (Figure 3). Evaluation tasks, accuracy metrics, and temperature zero remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix E and Figure 6 are removed, eliminating the dedicated 12-model confusion-matrix analysis testing whether class imbalance produces majority-class collapse. Reasoning-consistency experiments, visual-alignment cases, error-awareness comparisons, and few-shot analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the annotation-agreement procedure and a stratified 300-instance Cohen's kappa study. Neither introduces evaluation confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting. The changed kappa value is a result change, not a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: The ETC and EPD tables extensively update scores, rankings, and model entries. Headline accuracies change from 66.47% and 61.25% to 66.65% and 61.39%, respectively, under revised benchmark composition; these are not established same-setting gains. Auxiliary Doubao results replace o4-mini results, confusion-matrix results disappear, and annotation kappa changes from 0.794 to 0.796.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the same equally weighted standardized-feature score and Gaussian sampling formulation. No new mathematical definitions, assumptions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a benchmark for diagnosing multimodal reasoning errors. The introduction and conclusion narrow its interpretation to a controlled diagnostic stress-test, replacing broader suggestions of distinguishing sound from flawed reasoning. The claimed empirical survey changes from 20 to 12 models.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly states that all-error EPD cannot measure false positives on clean chains or full calibration, and explains why always predicting an error reduces to ETC-level performance. Results are reinterpreted around proprietary versus open-weight models instead of thinking mechanisms and scale. Auxiliary-subset comparability cautions are added, while the class-imbalance assurance is removed.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix C and Table 5 newly specify a randomly sampled 200-example few-shot subset and a shared subset and prompt template across shot settings. GPT-5.2 is explicitly labeled xhigh. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish that the corresponding settings changed.

R1.justification: Related work adds TRACE, video retrieval, fine-grained object detection, and attention-based hallucination studies, alongside changed model references. The central positioning against answer-oriented evaluation and step localization remains, with a narrower characterization of EPD.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much technical prose remain. Targeted rewrites update EPD framing, model descriptions, results, and conclusions; contributions become bullets, acknowledgments and corresponding-author information are added, and the appendices are reorganized.

P2.justification: The main comparison tables regroup and reorder models, replacing top-two bold/underline marking with top-three shading. The EPD table moves from v1 Appendix C to v2 main-text Table 2. Figures 2–4 are revised, the confusion-matrix figure is removed, and several captions gain explanatory detail.

improvement.justification: v2 narrows EPD's interpretation to what an all-error dataset can establish and clarifies auxiliary-subset reporting, resolving misleading justification and ambiguity in v1. These improve interpretation of the retained evidence. Removing the dedicated class-imbalance analysis weakens diagnostic support and limits the net gain; the revised headline scores do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.
